data.comentario_gestor: The Sub-Fund strategy is to invest in companies with strong fundamentals and undervalued share prices. This strategy worked well over the last 10 years. However, during the year 2024, the Sub-Fund's performance was lower due to a relatively worse market performance of European Small and Mid Cap listed companies. Money flows continued to go to large American companies and smaller European companies did not benefit from it. The Sub-Fund increased its exposure to several industries, with 11 new investments. The Sub-Fund opened positions on Midwich and EVS in the audiovisual technology sector, Ebro in branded food and Millenium, Just Eat and Ibersol in the hospitality industry. The Sub-Fund increased its exposure to the automotive industry through Stabilus and to the pet services market through CVS. The Sub-Fund sold Applus and TI Fluids Systems to their takeover bidders and sold Vopak, Do&Co and Wilh Wilhelmsen after achieving very good returns. At the end of the year, the Sub-Fund has a high upside potential as the majority of its investments were performing well and the valuation at which they are trading is significantly low. The Sub-Fund doesn't hold any defaulted or distressed securities. It also doesn't hold any static investments, as the valuations of the investments are regularly reviewed and changed. Exposure to emerging market equities remained steady throughout the year at around 3%. The Sub-Fund started the year with a long USD position of around 6%. As the USD rallied during the first half of the year, the exposure was increased in August. In the final quarter, it was reduced.
